md_docs_2testing_2coverage(3) Library Functions Manual md_docs_2testing_2coverage(3)

NAME

md_docs_2testing_2coverage - Native coverage

Coverage measures the C/C++ product sources compiled by the native test builds. It does not measure every platform or the browser build merely because their files exist in src/. Tests and vendored dependencies do not contribute to the product score. Keep untested product code in the report; do not exclude a module to satisfy a target.

Reading the numbers

The Codecov headline is fully covered lines divided by hits + misses + partials. An executed line with untested conditional branches can count as partial, so this score differs from gcovr's executed-line percentage. partials_as_hits stays disabled. Original Cobertura branch information is preserved in uploads.

Coverage builds explicitly disable sanitizers. Clang's gcov instrumentation otherwise counts sanitizer-generated guards as branches on plain assignments (for example settings->width = values->width), even though these are not source decisions. The separate Linux Debug sanitizer unit job retains ASan/UBSan checks with coverage disabled; normal Debug builds still enable sanitizers by default. Keep a matched measurement when distinguishing this reporting correction from newly exercised behavior.

The complete-upload summary records executed-line coverage for production code and separately for src/ (application). It unions line identities across the seven reports instead of averaging shard percentages or summing duplicate lines. Use Codecov's processed report for the branch-aware score.

Always compare the exact commit and report inventory. On November 2, 2026, Codecov's repository API still reported 39.62% from 237dce570 (October 22), while 9bfcf8c74, the then-current master, was pending without totals. That old report contained 371 files; src/ had 3,343 hits, 6,239 partials and 5,187 misses (14,769 lines). Its 22.64% fully covered score and 64.88% executed-line score describe different metrics. Neither establishes current-master coverage.

Policy in codecov.yml

Setting Policy and reason Default branch master, matching the repository Upload completion One upload after all seven native CI reports pass inventory validation; no carryforward Report age 24 hours, allowing a slow full matrix without accepting arbitrarily old reports Notifications Publish after that upload without waiting for unrelated statuses; report processing errors Overall project Compare with the base, allowing at most one percentage point of regression Application project At least 50% for src/, with zero threshold allowance Patch At least 60%; security patches at least 70%, with zero allowance Branch filters None: feature branches need checks and PR comments too Components Current module paths, baseline-relative informational project checks Flags Only coverage is a native coverage upload; per-job test analytics flags are independent Comments One updated comment including components, even if base coverage is unavailable Ignored files Build output, dependencies, test scaffolding, generated version and musl compatibility code Partials and annotations Retain branch partials and source annotations

The previous configuration duplicated module gates as components, omitted newer session/MCP/media/UI modules, had obsolete branch and upload flag lists, and included redundant paths such as lib/audio/audio.* beneath lib/audio/. The CI-success setting belongs directly under codecov, not under notify. The separate changes status is disabled; the project, application and patch checks provide the gates, and components diagnose module regressions.

Validate edits against Codecov's live schema:

curl --fail --data-binary @codecov.yml https://api.codecov.io/validate
python .github/scripts/test_generate_coverage.py
python .github/scripts/test_prepare_coverage_upload.py
python .github/scripts/test_criterion_to_junit.py

References: YAML reference, status checks, components.

Reproducing a local measurement

Use Clang, Ninja and a compatible glibc/Linux or macOS build tree. From Windows, use the repository's Linux test container. Share the main worktree's .deps-cache source/download cache, while keeping platform-specific compiled dependencies and instrumented objects in a separate build tree. 

GITHUB_CMAKE_BINARY_DIR=build_coverage cmake --preset github -B build_coverage -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \


  -DASCIICHAT_FORCE_CRITERION_TESTS=ON -DASCIICHAT_ENABLE_COVERAGE=ON \


  -DASCIICHAT_ENABLE_SANITIZERS=OFF -DUSE_MUSL=OFF
cmake --build build_coverage --target ascii-chat tests
# Remove only stale counters in this measurement's build tree before running.
find build_coverage -name '*.gcda' -delete
ctest --test-dir build_coverage -L '^(unit|integration|performance)$' \


  --no-tests=error --output-on-failure --parallel 2 \


  --output-junit Testing/coverage-tests.xml
python .github/scripts/generate-coverage.py \


  --build build_coverage --output build_coverage/coverage.xml

Record test failures and prerequisite skips alongside the report. Coverage generation or an accepted upload does not imply tests passed. A local Linux measurement is not evidence of native macOS/Windows execution or a substitute for the seven-shard CI completeness gate. When publishing a local measurement, identify its platform, build configuration, test scope and exact source commit.
